Judge: A wins clearly in all four pairs, and none of them is close. All four A frames have strong atmospheric depth: haze that separates the distance into layers, a sun or time of day you can read, and graded colour. They are dense and varied, with traffic, aircraft, people and mixed plants. Each is composed like a film shot, with a hero or landmark in the foreground framing the skyline. Three of the four genuinely impress; the midday golf frame is very good but plain. The B frames share the same faults across the board: flat water in a single tone with no reflections; flat light with no clear direction under a smeared sky texture; distant skylines no softer than nearby buildings, so the city looks like a model; heavily repeated building and tree models; empty streets and promenades; and a HUD with a placeholder minimap. B's best frame is the ground-level crossing (pair 3), where the character model, warm low sun and tree canopy are respectable, but the empty asphalt kills it. To close the gap, B needs these fixes in order: (1) water shading with reflections and glint, (2) haze layering by distance and a directional key light with a proper sky, (3) traffic and pedestrian density at a readable scale, (4) more varied assets and better framing of landmarks.
